correctness.rationale: Full proof reconstructed for all k>=2 and R>0. Gauge of symmetric cyclic polygon gives equality of the actual hull with the set x²+g_Q(y)²<=R². Fubini yields V=4R³ A(Q)/3. Explicit Jacobian 2sin(gamma/2) sqrt(1-x²sin²(gamma/2)) integrates to gamma+sin gamma per ruled side, with measure-zero seams and endpoints; hence S=R²(2pi+2A(Q)). Jensen strict concavity over positive gaps totaling pi gives the unique equiangular maximum and sharp unattained infima. Standalone verify.py compares independent sampled disk hulls with closed formulas, uses separate Gaussian quadrature, and checks random gap optimality. It returned VERIFY_OK; finite verification is supplementary, not a proof.

originality.rationale: The closest primary full-text calculation is Finch (arXiv:1211.4514, Section 1), which proves exactly the k=2 perpendicular pair V=8/3 and S=2(2+pi) and is expressly excluded from novelty. Bäsel (arXiv:1604.07245) studies displaced-center oloid geometry. Nash et al. (arXiv:1612.09382) classify hull face lattices and edge algebraic structure for two circles; they do not give the all-k surface/volume identity or strict equal-gap extremizers. Published mathematical-record comparisons did not find a covering assertion. Unindexed pre-existing derivations remain possible; lack of matches alone is not treated as proof.
residual_risks: The k=2 perpendicular right-angle case, including both intrinsic-volume constants, is explicitly known and is not a novelty contribution.
An earlier unindexed study of multi-disk convex hulls or a general ruled-surface integral theorem could contain equivalent all-k formulas.
Published mathematical record and accessible files are not an exhaustive priority check or a guarantee against unpublished work.

value.rationale: The family is a canonical arbitrary finite collection of great disks generalizing a classical pair. The exact affine surface-volume relation across all angular data and all cardinalities makes two distinct intrinsic volumes depend on one small invariant, with a sharp joint maximizer and equality classification. This is nontrivial geometric information, requires a global hull description and ruled patch integrals, and yields a ball-approximation sequence; no blanket theorem about displaced circles or general convex bodies is claimed.
